deficiencies.description: The text states that biologists studying tumours often explant the tumour, and then separately states that the audience is looking at a slice through a tumour and a stain to look at morphology. The rewrite states that the slice through a tumour 'illustrates this', linking the slice to the explanting of the tumour, which the text does not state.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: often they will explant the tumor. Here you're looking at a slice through a tumor and a stain to look at the morphology.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: A slice through a tumour, with a stain to show the morphology, illustrates this [FIGURE].

considerations.sourcePassage: Primary cells really don't grow in culture.
considerations.reason: Dropping 'really' removes conversational emphasis rather than a scientific hedge, as the lecturer previously stated that 'all of those cells will not grow'.

considerations.sourcePassage: Whoops, I forgot to start my clock. Okay.
considerations.reason: Omitted as an aside/remark about the lecture.

considerations.sourcePassage: what I want you to appreciate is that by just studying one cell in a dish, you're not really getting a full picture of exactly what's gone on in this tumor with regard to the contributions of things like the stroma and other things.
considerations.reason: The conversational framing 'what I want you to appreciate is that' is an allowed omission of remarks to the audience, and 'other components' has the same meaning as 'other things'.
